create.name: Amrit Yoga Institute
create.bio:
Set in Salt Springs, the Amrit Yoga Institute is a charitable yoga school and ashram, among the forests of north-central Florida. It was founded by Yogi Amrit Desai, known to students as Gurudev Shri Amritji. A disciple of Swami Kripalu, he was among the first teachers to bring yoga to America from India, and the institute carries on his approach, called I AM Yoga, which treats postures, breath and attention as a single meditative practice rather than physical exercise alone. His daughter Kamini Desai leads much of its yoga nidra and training work, alongside a group of long-standing faculty.

The campus runs residential immersions and retreats through the year, on themes such as meditation in motion, the Yoga Sutras of Patanjali, yoga nidra and bringing yogic principles into working life, as well as yoga teacher trainings at several levels, kirtan and chanting, and initiation retreats in the lineage of Swami Kripalu. Each week it holds a Friday meditation and a Sunday practice and discourse with Amritji, open in person and by livestream. Recorded courses, a streaming service and a YouTube channel of short talks on consciousness, the ego and the Bhagavad Gita carry its teaching further afield.

courses.title: December Community Overnight Retreat
courses.description: A one-night community retreat on the Salt Springs campus with satsang, evening and morning sessions and time with Amritji. Lodging, dinner and breakfast are included.

courses.title: I AM Yoga® Meditation in Motion® Immersion
courses.description: A six-day residential immersion with Indu Heather Arena and Amritji in the institute's signature practice, where hatha postures are held as moving meditation. Prices depend on the room chosen.
courses.price: From $899 USD (local, no lodging) to $1,539 USD

courses.title: I AM Yoga® Yoga Sutras Immersion Retreat
courses.description: Five days of study and practice of Patanjali's Yoga Sutras with Nirali Lauren McCrea and Amritji at the Florida campus. The hours count towards a 200-hour teacher training.

courses.title: Spirit at Work: Bringing the Wisdom of Yoga into the World of Work
courses.description: A five-day programme with Kamini Desai and Amritji on applying yogic ideas about energy and attention to professional life, so that work comes from presence rather than pressure.
courses.price: From $799 USD (local, no lodging) to $1,439 USD

courses.title: The Yoga Nidra Deep Dive
courses.description: A weekend immersion in yoga nidra with John Vosler, mixing sessions, guided practice and a closing darshan with Amritji.
courses.price: From $399 USD (local, no lodging) to $1,039 USD

free_resources.title: Amrit Yoga Institute on Insight Timer
free_resources.description: The institute's teacher page on the free Insight Timer app, with its recorded meditations and yoga nidra practices.

free_resources.title: Weekly Meditation and Discourse with Gurudev
free_resources.description: A Friday half-hour meditation and a Sunday hour of discourse with Amritji, plus a Sunday all-levels practice, open in person at the ashram or by livestream.

flags: Listed as a school (entity_type school), not an individual: the queue entry is the institute's own Insight Timer channel. Owner may prefer to hold organisations until the organisations shelf rule applies.
Possible overlap: Kamini Desai (Amrit Desai's daughter) is already on Spiritpedia (kamini-desai) and leads several of the institute's programmes; she is mentioned in the bio.
Email [email removed] is an organisation inbox, shown via Cloudflare email protection (decoded, clickable mailto) on the contact page; the same page has a contact form.
Base: Salt Springs, Florida (campus address on the contact page, recorded at town level only); Salt Springs is a small community (likely under 5,000 people), please map it.
Regional: north-central Florida (Marion County, near Ocala), outside the big coastal cities.
Only one photo: a 400px headshot of the founder, Gurudev Shri Amritji (Yogi Amrit Desai), from the institute's site; other site images are icons, logos or a blurred class photo.
Tier: the founder is a well-known figure in American yoga (editorial stature could be argued); not raised, owner decides.
For the owner's awareness: Amrit Desai left Kripalu in 1994 after admitting sexual relationships with students; this is public history, not mentioned in the bio.
YouTube titles copied as shown (some contain double spaces where the channel uses them); the channel also posts very short clips, which were left out.
Owner, 12 Nov 2026: the email had been decoded from Cloudflare protection; removed on dev and live (contact form kept where there is one).
